mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing discount rates on future corporate earnings and increasing equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of declining FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% over the past 3 months signals weakening labor market conditions, which increases the probability of future monetary policy easing and reduces inflation expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and personal consumption (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening in private demand, which increases the likelihood of central bank intervention and triggers a risk-on rally in equities over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline (t-test p > 0.05) or interaction Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in real output, which raises concerns about near-term recession and triggers a flight to quality, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate policy support.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO falls below 105.0 (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the growth rate of real personal consumption (RSAFS) combined with a stable or declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals strong underlying demand momentum, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both RSAFS growth exceeds 0.8% MoM and UNRATE < 6.8% (t-test p > 0.05) or interaction Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% per annum, combined with a stable or rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 216.5), signals a tightening monetary policy regime that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 216.5 (t-test p > 0.05) or interaction Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) below 50k per month, combined with a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE > 6.6%), indicates labor market weakening, which increases the probability of future rate cuts and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: labor market softening with rising unemployment
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS growth < 50k and UNRATE > 6.6% (t-test p > 0.05) or interaction Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in real GDP (GDPC1) over the past 5 months, combined with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO), signals a broad-based economic slowdown, which increases the likelihood of fiscal or monetary stimulus and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 growth < 0.5% and INDPRO < 106.0 (t-test p > 0.05) or interaction Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
